reason: The abstract reports associations of nighttime fasting and breakfast timing with prostate cancer overall. It does not analyze an aggressive prostate cancer incidence endpoint. The total analytic sample is not explicitly stated and was not inferred by summing cases and controls.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: After controlling for time of breakfast, fasting for more than 11 h overnight (the median duration among controls) was associated with a reduced risk of prostate cancer compared to those fasting for 11 h or less (OR = 0.77, 95% 0.54-1.07).
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate is for prostate cancer overall and contains no aggressive-disease restriction.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Combining a long nighttime fasting and an early breakfast was associated with a lower risk of prostate cancer compared to a short nighttime fasting and a late breakfast (OR = 0.54, 95% CI 0.27-1.04).
estimate_classifications.reason: The combined fasting and breakfast-timing estimate is for prostate cancer overall, without an aggressive endpoint definition.
